sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and logger setup
sections.what: Loads the JSON, hashing, path, time, settings, and logger tools.
sections.why: Likely reason: needed to save state and build fingerprints.

sections.name: IndexState (part 1)
sections.title: State loading, saving and fingerprint
sections.what: Creates a tracker for one collection, loads its state file or starts empty, saves the state, and builds a fingerprint from a file's path and modified time.
sections.why: Likely reason: one state file per collection keeps collections separate.
sections.watch_out: A damaged or unreadable state file is silently replaced by an empty one, so the next run processes every file again.

sections.name: IndexState: is_indexed
sections.title: Indexed file checks and updates
sections.what: Answers whether a file is already indexed with the same fingerprint, records newly indexed files, lists indexed files, returns a file's record, removes a file, and summarises the totals.
sections.why: Likely reason: the indexer uses these to decide what to skip and to report progress.
sections.watch_out: The fingerprint ignores file content, so a file changed without a new modified time is treated as unchanged.

sections.name: IndexState: clear
sections.title: Clear all state
sections.what: Resets the tracker to an empty record and saves that empty record to the file.
sections.why: Likely reason: used when a collection is rebuilt from scratch.
sections.watch_out: Clearing forgets every file, so the next run re-processes everything. It only resets the state file and does not remove stored vectors.

summary: Keeps a record of which documents were indexed and a fingerprint for each, so unchanged files are skipped on the next run.
purpose: Saves time and cost by avoiding indexing files that have not changed.
why: Likely reason: indexing is slow and costly, so repeating it for unchanged files is wasteful.
how: Loads the collection's state file or starts empty. For each file, it makes a fingerprint from the path and last modified time. It stores the fingerprint when a file is indexed, checks it on later runs, and saves the file after each change.
inputs: A file path, its last modified text, and the collection name.
outputs: Yes or no answers, a list of indexed files, a summary of counts, and the state file on disk.
risks: The fingerprint uses only the path and modified time, so an edit that keeps the same time is missed. A damaged state file is silently replaced by an empty one, which triggers a full re-index. Saving after every file slows large runs, and no lock is visible in this file.
debug: Find index_state.json in the collection folder under the vector store path. Check logs for Error loading index state or already indexed lines. If everything re-indexes each run, check that the file exists and is valid JSON.
